property_summary: Whenever the pseudo-random draw yields 0, the player wins and the pot must be paid out and reset to 0; the mutant pays out only on random==1, so for a draw of 0 the pot stays at 10 instead of 0.

For any caller and any block environment, a play whose draw is 0 must empty the pot and the contract's ether balance; the mutant pays out on draw 1 instead, so on a draw of 0 it leaves pot/balance nonzero.
Whenever a play's pseudo-random draw equals 0 (a winning play), the pot must be fully paid out and reset to 0; the mutant pays out only on draw 1, so for a draw-0 play it leaves pot at 10.

For any actor and block environment, a play whose pseudo-random draw is 0 is a winning play and must leave c.pot() == 0; the mutant pays out only on draw 1, so on a draw-0 play it leaves the pot at 10.
For any winning play (draw 0) with the exact ticket price from an EOA, the pot must be fully paid out and reset to 0; the mutant pays out only on draw 1, leaving the pot nonzero on such plays.

For any caller and any block timestamp, play() awards the pot (pot becomes 0) exactly when keccak(timestamp,difficulty,caller) % 2 == 0; the % 3 mutant fails to award (pot stays 10) whenever that hash % 3 == 2, breaking the rule.

For any player address and timestamp, whenever keccak256(timestamp,difficulty,player) % 2 == 0 the play wins and pot() must end at 0; the %3 mutant leaves pot at 10 for such inputs whenever that hash % 3 == 2.

For any player and timestamp, whenever keccak256(timestamp,difficulty,player) % 2 != 0 the reference C does NOT pay out, so pot() stays at 10; the %3 mutant pays out whenever that hash % 3 == 0 (which implies %2 != 0), leaving pot() at 0 and breaking the rule.
A second winning-or-losing play() must never revert: because the pot is credited with each ticket, the payout `pot - FEE` cannot underflow, whereas in the mutant the pot stays 0 and a win reverts.
